radiology_report:
Radiology Division | Gelderse Vallei Hospital, Ede | 15 January 2025
Exam: multiparametric MRI prostate

Clinical indication:
Elevated prostate-specific antigen trending upward, specifically PSA value: 18.0 ng/mL, warrants assessment for clinically significant prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
The gland is hypertrophied, occupying 94.6 mL of pelvic volume. T2 sequences highlight a discrete hypointense focus at the left peripheral zone, spanning the base to mid-region, spanning 18 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by low ADC signal. Post-contrast dynamics exhibit prompt, focal enhancement against adjacent tissue. Capsular integrity remains intact with no seminal vesicle penetration. Benign prostatic hyperplasia dominates the central zone, featuring a moderately enlarged median lobe. Pelvic nodes appear unremarkable, and skeletal survey reveals no osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS: 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone (base/mid), measuring approximately 18 mm.
Prostate volume: 94.6 mL; PSA density: 0.19 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa probability: 0.51321477.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Laboratory tracking from June 2024 documented a prostate-specific antigen concentration of 14.8 ng/mL, triggering a repeat assay and advanced imaging referral. Clinical discussion centered on the necessity for specialized urological assessment given the upward trajectory and current presentation. A subsequent visit has been arranged to evaluate the magnetic resonance outcomes.
